A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety, utility, inference-speed, and ablation results in Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Llama3 evaluations and engagement-score experiments in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The speculative decoding procedure, match-ratio switching, sampling distributions, and parameter updates remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2. The Llama3 experiments apply the existing method to another model configuration.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C evaluates another model pair on retained prefilling and utility tasks; Appendix D analyzes existing utility data and responses.

E2.justification: All existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. The added Llama3 experiments use the already evaluated No Defense and Deep-Align baselines. Appendix D's utility-only model serves as an analysis control.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a Llama3.1-8b-Instruct target with a Llama3.2-1b-Instruct expert. Appendix D introduces utility-only fine-tuning and prompt-based output-length controls. Previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused investigation of Deep-Align's high Vicuna engagement score through response examples, utility-only fine-tuning, and output-length controls. Existing strength-parameter analyses and jailbreak robustness tests remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical results in the original six tables are retained. Tables 7–8 add results for one Llama3 model pair: GSM8K scores are 81.8% without defense, 75.2% for SSD, and 10.3% for Deep-Align. Appendix D adds response-style and engagement-control findings, including a 4.46 engagement score after utility-only fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that SSD transfers deep safety alignment without tuning the target model, preserves utility, and accelerates inference. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes Deep-Align's high engagement score primarily to conversational style encouraged by its utility training data, with response length considered a smaller contributor. The stated model-size and target/expert conversational-style limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 reports that an implementation is available and supplies a repository address in Section 5. v2 also identifies the additional model checkpoints and describes the new controls, although detailed training settings and length-control prompts are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dubey et al. (2024), The Llama 3 Herd of Models, for the additional model evaluation. The related-work discussion and positioning against prior defense and controllable-generation methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 moves the over-refusal discussion ahead of inference efficiency, adds Appendices C–D and an acknowledgment, and makes localized wording, affiliation-order, and cross-reference edits. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–10 and an explanatory footnote to Table 2, exchanges the placement and numbering of the former Tables 3–4, and repositions Table 6. The three figures and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: The Llama3 evaluation, focused engagement-score controls, and code-release information modestly strengthen empirical support and transparency. The gains are limited by incomplete details for the added experiments and an unexplained difference between Table 2's engagement score of 4.36 and Table 10's 227-word result of 4.42.
